doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Did bands change their repertoire for the colored night?
summary: He thinks bands played their hits and varied by tempo; mentions Vaughn Monroe and Alvino Rey.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: You probably have no way of knowing this, but do you think that bands would change their songlist from the white night to the colored night?

That’s a good question. Not going to the white night band, I think they played their recorded hits, whatever their records were. Because with Krupa, he just played everything he played. Well a lot of it had to do with tempo, see the dance tempo. A lot of it was that. And all the bands sounded good. Heck. Vaughn Monroe’s band, they came into the T&D Theater and he had an excellent band. There was a sweet band. Alvino Rey, guitarist, he was with Horace Heidt who was the house band at the Golden Gate Theater for many years, and then when that band, Horace Heidt split, why Alvino Rey formed his own band and he came up from Los Angeles. He played the T&D Theater. They had a good band. I’m just trying to think of the other bands that I saw.
